::: {#thm-binary-size}
#### A short binary tree has few vertices

For every binary tree $T$ (@def-binary-tree), with size and height as in @rem-size-height,

$$
\operatorname{size}(T) \le 2^{\operatorname{height}(T) + 1} - 1.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

We use structural induction (@def-structural-induction) on $T$.

**Base case.**
$\operatorname{size}(\mathtt{nil}) = 0 = 2^{-1 + 1} - 1$.

**Inductive step.**
Let $T = \operatorname{node}(x, L, R)$, where $L$ and $R$ satisfy the inequality, and let $h = \operatorname{height}(T)$.
By @rem-size-height, $\operatorname{height}(L) \le h - 1$ and $\operatorname{height}(R) \le h - 1$.
Then, using the formula for size in @rem-size-height first,

$$
\ba
\operatorname{size}(T)
&= 1 + \operatorname{size}(L) + \operatorname{size}(R)
&& \text{(formula for size)}
\\&\le 1 + \paren{2^{\operatorname{height}(L) + 1} - 1} + \paren{2^{\operatorname{height}(R) + 1} - 1}
&& \text{(induction hypothesis)}
\\&\le 1 + \paren{2^{h} - 1} + \paren{2^{h} - 1}
\\&= 2^{h + 1} - 1.
\ea
$$

By structural induction, the inequality holds for every binary tree.

:::

:::
